thread:
customer_netadmin: Hey team — since y'day afternoon we've been seeing sporadic mTLS handshake failures from our VPC to Redwood Private control plane. ~10% of connections fail with TLS alert and client hello retries. Only impacts control plane endpoint, not other services.
sam_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact error seen on your side (tcpdump/openssl)?
customer_netadmin: Logs show `tlsv1 alert decode_error` and some `handshake_failure` entries. Here's a short tcpdump excerpt:```17:48:02.123456 IP src=10.12.3.44 dst=34.201.86.123 tcp 76 [SYN]``` then clienthello fragments, then RST. Also saw DNS timeouts to controlplane-rr internal CNAME sometimes.
jia_eng: A couple of quick checks: 1) Are you doing egress inspection/SSL intercept? 2) Any MTU or fragmentation changes on the NAT? 3) Did you rotate any CA bundles or mTLS certs recently?
customer_netadmin: We did push a firewall upgrade and tightened egress allowlist last night. No cert rotations on our side. No explicit SSL intercept but an NGFW does TLS fingerprinting. MTU unchanged.
emma_ops: Deploy-bot just reported a control plane cert rotation this morning (normal rotation): `deploy-bot: control-plane/certs rotated at 04:10 UTC`. Might be relevant if your NGFW caches certs.
sam_support: Thanks — can you run a reproducible client test and include the SNI and ALPN from the clienthello? Example command:```openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood.example:443 -servername controlplane.redwood.example -msg -state``` That will show handshake trace.
customer_netadmin: Ran it, attached output snippet: `ClientHello SNI=controlplane.redwood.example, alpn=h2,http/1.1, cipher=TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`. Handshake completes ~90% but fails with `TLS alert decode_error` intermittently.
jia_eng: Two hypotheses: 1) NGFW doing TLS inspection/mangling on first handshake after cert rotation; 2) UDP fragmentation for large ClientHello (EDNS size) causing server to see truncated SNI leading to decode_error. Can you capture full pcap of a failing and succeeding flow? Look for TCP MSS/DF, IP id, fragmentation flags.
customer_netadmin: Captured both. Failing flows show clienthello split across TCP segments then server RST. Also saw an intermediate NAT rewriting total length on one path.
sam_support: If the NGFW is reassembling incorrectly or dropping segments, that could produce decode_error. Workarounds: - allow passthrough for controlplane IP ranges and ports - disable TLS fingerprinting for that rule - temporarily bypass the NGFW for those hosts
emma_ops: Also check DNS path — if you get a stale/misconfigured CNAME (short TTL) you might be hitting a different controlplane egress IP that the NGFW treats differently. Can you `dig +trace` and share TTLs?
customer_netadmin: Dig shows controlplane -> cp-rr.example.redwood.net CNAME, TTL 30s. There were TTL misses during our firewall rollout.
jia_eng: Action plan: 1) Customer to whitelist controlplane IP ranges and disable TLS inspection for that host group (short-term). 2) Collect pcap and share with us (redact IPs if needed). 3) We'll correlate with our ingress logs for the rotation window and verify if any old certs still being served by edge nodes.
sam_support: Also try increasing client handshake timeout to 10s as a temporary mitigation — gives more time for reassembly behind the NGFW.
customer_netadmin: Will do whitelist and bypass for a subset of a host pool and report back in ~30m. Thanks. :pray:
(30m later) customer_netadmin: After bypassing NGFW for test hosts, handshakes are stable, 0 failures in 1000 connections.
jia_eng: Great — that strongly implicates the NGFW. We double-checked our cert rollout: all active edge nodes serving the new cert after rotation. No config anomalies on our side.
emma_ops: Filing an advisory: recommend customers with TLS-inspecting NGFWs to allow direct egress to controlplane IP ranges during certificate rotations and to avoid caching cert-related state. We'll add a KB article.
sam_support: Marking this as mitigated for now. If you can share a sanitized pcap we can file a bug with the NGFW vendor with packet-level evidence.
customer_netadmin: Will send sanitized pcap and firewall rule dump. Appreciate the quick help, folks. :tada:
